title: Sonam Wangchuk says he is under house arrest before Ladakh's winter local polls
dek: Police say he was advised to stay home under prohibitory orders for the elections. Protesters want the 21 November and 4 December polls rethought and an inquiry report released.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk said on Friday that he had been placed under house arrest at his home in Leh, days before local body elections in Ladakh that protesters want postponed. "I AM UNDER HOUSE ARREST," he wrote on social media, and said he would approach the magistrate, the High Court and, if needed, the Supreme Court.

About 20 to 25 armed police and paramilitary personnel have been posted outside his residence since Wednesday night, according to Mr Wangchuk and reports. Police removed him from a sit-in on Wednesday.

## What the police say

Ladakh Police said Mr Wangchuk had been "advised to stay at home", not arrested, according to reports. The force said the measures follow prohibitory orders issued by the Union Territory's Chief Electoral Officer and the Leh District Magistrate, which regulate rallies and gatherings in the Leh municipal area during the election period.

## The elections

Ladakh's Chief Secretary, Ashish Kundra, announced on 10 November that elections to the Leh and Kargil municipal councils and to panchayats will be held on 21 November, and polls to the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council on 4 December, according to reports.

Protesters, including groups linked to the Leh Apex Body and the Kargil Democratic Alliance, want the government to rethink holding the polls in winter, when many residents leave the region for the plains. Some groups have called for a boycott. They are also demanding the release of the report of the commission of inquiry into the violence in Leh on 24 September 2025, in which four people were killed when police opened fire on protesters.

## Background

Ladakh became a Union Territory without a legislature when Jammu and Kashmir's special status was revoked in August 2019. Since then the Leh Apex Body and the Kargil Democratic Alliance have campaigned for statehood and for Ladakh to be brought under the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution, which gives tribal areas autonomous councils with powers over land and local laws.

Mr Wangchuk was detained under the National Security Act after the September 2025 violence, which the authorities blamed on his speeches; he denied inciting it. The Centre has held several rounds of talks with Ladakh's leaders through a high-powered committee of the Ministry of Home Affairs.

The Ladakh administration and the Ministry of Home Affairs have not commented beyond the police statement. No party in Parliament had responded publicly by Saturday morning.

## What happens next

If Mr Wangchuk files a legal challenge, the first hearing would be before a magistrate in Leh or the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh. Voting for the municipal councils and panchayats is due in a week, on 21 November.
